description: A translucent rounded panel with a light border and a shadow, blurring and saturating the colored shapes behind it: the basic glass surface.

florui.css: .scene { position: relative; width: 200px; height: 140px; background-color: #1b1b2f; overflow: hidden; } .s1 { position: absolute; left: 10px; top: 10px; width: 90px; height: 90px; background-color: #ff5a5f; border-radius: 45px; } .s2 { position: absolute; left: 80px; top: 50px; width: 100px; height: 70px; background-color: #2ec4b6; } .s3 { position: absolute; left: 20px; top: 90px; width: 70px; height: 40px; background-color: #ffd166; } .glass { position: absolute; left: 40px; top: 30px; width: 120px; height: 80px; border-radius: 20px; background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4); box-shadow: 0px 8px 24px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35); backdrop-filter: blur(8px) saturate(1.5); }

classification.reason: Chromium and this engine build a Gaussian blur differently (kernel shape and rounding), so a pixel in the blurred area differs by a few levels of 255 and a pixel at a steep colour edge by more. Measured against desktop Chrome: 0.54% of pixels differ by more than 8 levels (43% by any amount, mean error 0.8, max 26), geometry an exact match. channel_tolerance 8 stops the harmless rounding from counting; the percentage left is the steep edges. With the backdrop blur read past the panel edge as transparent instead of mirrored (the defect this fixture found), about 30% of the pixels differed by more than that.
